title: Swim in Rising Water
statement:
You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `grid` where each value `grid[i][j]` represents the elevation at that point `(i, j)`.
The rain starts to fall. At time `t`, the depth of the water everywhere is `t`. You can swim from a square to another 4-directionally adjacent square if and only if the elevation of both squares individually are at most `t`.
You can swim infinite distances in zero time. Of course, you must stay within the boundaries of the grid during your swim.
Return the least time until you can reach the bottom right square `(n - 1, n - 1)` if you start at the top left square `(0, 0)`.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer n.
Next n lines: n space-separated integers.
constraints:
n == grid.length
n == grid[i].length
1 <= n <= 50
0 <= grid[i][j] < n^2
Each value grid[i][j] is unique.

examples.explanation: At time 3, all squares are reachable. Shortest max elevation path is 0->1->3.
Minimum maximum height in path is 16.
